approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves scored molecular graphs through score-band parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and local mutation. Stable canonical admission creates a surplus pool. A Gaussian process learns from every earlier accepted raw score using folded counts of radius-two molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity. It chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws, then updates the archive, breeding population and incumbent using real raw scores.
approach.novelty: Add a fixed topological atom-pair count channel alongside the retained local counts, and average their separately normalized similarity kernels equally. Atom types separated by graph distances up to thirty bonds can provide relational information missing from local environment counts. Earlier unfolding kept the same local environments, while ordinal targets changed label spacing; both lost mean endpoint score. This tests additional molecular information through one fixed covariance composition, with raw-score targets and the search rules retained. Added information may also dilute useful locality, so alias splitting or better prediction alone will not establish benefit.

observed_bottleneck: The current count GP can assign identical representation to distinct molecular graphs and cannot encode every nonlocal arrangement. This is a representational limitation and a candidate causal obstacle, not proof that adding features improves search. Actual summaries/run logs give n-62daf219c70a a complete mean of 0.5956696497334577 with population SD 0.02659287062806747, all fifteen sessions complete and 4,350 accepted offspring. The current matched multiplicity removal n-e00db808bbb4 loses 0.051295849138213355 on mean and every seed macro, with three contrary task-seed gains, supporting retaining local counts under its literal conditions. Its repeated binary histories add no independent seeds. The historical count implementations n-559d25e9c9c7 and n-98e8cdf5c51d implement the same count principle and reproduce the same complete 0.574343936523512 score on their older Parent; their +0.022573281535690642 comparison is not a new current-Parent gain or independent replication. Counts changed ordinary similarity weighting while actual local aliases remained. The failed unfolding n-b14daceabbeb changed all 435 kernels and 392 selected sets yet lost 0.04816296717262832 on complete mean and every seed macro; six task-seed endpoints, including all median_2 endpoints, improved. Nine distinct pairs remained equal in native and folded counts across actual training/cross/pool operands. Slight selected-stream prediction/coverage improvements did not establish endpoint gain; all median_2 MSEs worsened despite endpoint gains. The failed ordinal variant n-ae12ccae8c7b changed all actual 435 selected sets but lost 0.021067064526871015, with loss/gain/loss seed signs and six contrary task-seed gains. Its selected-stream mean rank correlation fell from passive raw 0.48429892962973947 to latent 0.4431662971746234, even while parent beats/incumbent gains increased to 655/272 and all median_2 endpoints improved. Its six published pool count-equivalent distinct pairs remain a representation limitation; the wider joint-operand audit below separates their scope from additional training/cross pairs. Ordinal units cannot establish raw-score calibration. The separate single-seed ridge/MILP degree-pair source n-0a6e29afd7f7 split 556 of 705 older descriptor alias pairs, including 507 of 625 with unequal labels, and changed construction preferences. Its own screening mean rose only 0.010270358917756017, while two tasks lost, AUC fell, MAE worsened, average source-relative gain stayed negative and runtime increased. It supplies omitted-information motivation, not GP, atom-pair, current-profile or multi-seed efficacy. A no-oracle audit of all 435 actual Parent archives/pools and original normal arrays freezes the prescribed atom-pair generator before evaluation and tests only one equal-weight composition. All 435 training, 435 cross and 435 pool Gram blocks change; 429 selected orders and 429 sets change on these unscored fixed inputs. Parent alias scope contains 0 distinct local-count pairs: 0 split and 0 remain under atom-pair counts. Of the nine unfolding-source pairs, 9 split and 0 remain; of 9 ordinal-source joint-operand pairs, 9 split and 0 remain. The ordinal joint audit counts 51 occurrences (six pool, three cross and 42 training), and its six pool pairs exactly match the six published pairs; three additional unique pairs occur outside pools. These conditional source-only distinctions establish potential exposure, not scored counterfactuals or a required future split frequency. Both failed scope assertions are retained: initially seven pool-only unfolding pairs were compared with nine joint-operand pairs, then nine joint-operand ordinal pairs were compared with six published pool pairs. Correcting these audit scopes changed no descriptor parameter, source evidence or scientific proposal.
hypothesis: Retain the Parent's local Morgan occurrence-count covariance and add sparse topological atom-pair occurrence-count covariance, using the fixed equal-weight average of their separate generalized Tanimoto kernels for every GP block while preserving raw-score learning and the inherited search rules.

finding_summary.headline: Atom-pair information changed search and split six local aliases, but the mean endpoint fell by 0.033408
finding_summary.insights: More descriptor distinctions and better predictions on selected molecules did not yield better endpoint search in this fixed mixture. On the actual accepted stream, raw MSE improved from 0.009475 for the passive local model to 0.009335, and mean batch ordering correlation rose from 0.545819 to 0.571243, despite the endpoint loss. These improvements were uneven: MSE worsened in seven task/seed cells, including all median_2 cells. Ordinary similarity and regularization changes were broadly exposed, whereas alias-mediated benefit was not: ten members of five split pool pairs remained unscored, and only one member of the cross pair was evaluated. Thirteen other pairs shared atom-pair counts but remained distinguishable through local counts; the channels still do not establish complete molecular identity. The negative result belongs to this one equal-weight composition and does not undo the earlier evidence for retaining local occurrence counts or isolate atom-pair information from mixture weighting. Molecular evidence still shows reactive heteroatom-halogen and sulfur motifs, large linked assemblies and destructive fragments alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. Added topological information does not enforce chemical feasibility, and neither a universal size explanation nor an alias-resolution explanation is established.
finding_summary.results: All 435 batches changed their raw posterior means, uncertainties and conditional covariance. Against the same-input local-only reference, 432 selected sets and 433 orders changed; three sets and two orders remained unchanged. All six distinct local-count alias pairs split, but none had both members scored. All three matched replicas completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.562261, a loss of 0.033408 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were −0.072325, +0.009185 and −0.037084. Six of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved: all three zaleplon results and the seed-1 deco_hop, drd2 and sitagliptin results. Every median_2 result declined. Seed dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.006995 around the lower mean. The mechanism ran correctly; its registered endpoint-benefit prediction was falsified.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, aza heterocycles and aryl amines persist; reactive bonds and unresolved ring geometry remain
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent trajectory files were read: Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task/seed, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per task. No task or Parent path is missing. The fresh brief marks both Child completion and matched Parent pairing complete, with no profile mismatches; the comparison is to n-62daf219c70a. The evaluated output contains compact fused aromatic carboxamides, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles, polycyclic aryl amines, aromatic lactam/urea assemblies and fluorinated unsaturated nitrogen-carbonyl rings. Ring-closure text incidence is 0.9529 to 0.9805 and aromatic-text incidence 0.9276 to 0.977. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. All stereocentre-text rates are zero. Charge-text incidence is zero except for one charge-separated nitrogen motif in the aromatic-amide task, rate 0.0011; neutral representations still contain basic amines. The chemical reading is rich rings/aromaticity, questionable synthetic plausibility, weak overall drug-likeness and moderate structural diversity across seeds, with narrower families among leaders within a seed. Conventional functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, unusual sulfur-H oxo environments and difficult bridges. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established. Sizes below are heavy-atom-token counts from the actual SMILES, not geometric measurements. The trajectory/offspring audit joins all 4,350 accepted offspring to their raw score, actual selected pool position and earlier evaluated parents. All fifteen raw-score leaders were evaluated and immediately admitted as survivors, and their scores agree with final best_so_far records. Immediate admission does not establish that every other evaluated molecule survives later replacement. The digest's final excerpt is a late seed-2 proposal list, not the retained leader of each seed. Full pool logs, rather than evaluated-only trajectories, support the pool observations below. Logged descriptors preserve the distinction between retained folded local Morgan counts and the added native sparse atom-pair counts. The receipts specify chirality-aware two-dimensional distances 1 through 30 and a fixed equal average of separately normalized count-Tanimoto kernels. Six distinct local-count-equal pairs occur in core training/cross/pool operands: five within-pool pairs and one archive-to-pool pair seen twice, hence seven occurrences; training contributes none. All six have unequal atom-pair rows and mixed similarity below one. Five additional pool_equivalence records repeat the five pool pairs and are not new pairs or independent observations. No distinct pair remains equal in both channels in these logged operands. This absence is conditional on the actual panel, not proof of molecular uniqueness. None of the ten members of the five within-pool pairs was evaluated in its task/seed. The cross pair has only one evaluated member: the 80-heavy-atom nitrogen-dione assembly in seed 2/evaluation 239 of the linked-heterocycle task, score 0.5910185045885361, immediately admitted but not an incumbent improvement. Its other member has no raw label. The six splits therefore supply no paired scored comparison. Conversely, thirteen distinct pairs remain equal in the atom-pair component alone while local counts distinguish them. Ten involve different single atoms with empty atom-pair rows; three involve sulfur-H or ring-bond variants. Their mixed similarities are below one, so component equality must not be called mixed-kernel equality. Finite identifiers, equal descriptor multisets, unspecified stereochemistry and restricted two-dimensional distances still limit identity and feasibility claims. The 435 passive local-only records explicitly have no alternative labels. Their predictions and choices are not another scored search, and a component or mixed similarity change does not demonstrate chemical benefit or mediation. Active posterior means are reported in raw-score units, covariance/noise in standardized raw-score units; the accepted labels and endpoint scores used here remain raw. Nothing here establishes global calibration. Historical applicability is retained as stated in the immutable brief: unfolding's nine unique aliases use joint training/cross/pool scope, whereas its seven within-pool occurrences are a narrower count; ordinal's six published pool pairs differ from the wider nine unique pairs across 51 joint occurrences. Their source-only atom-pair splits are conditional opportunity evidence, not current Child frequency, extra oracle outcomes or independent efficacy. Historical count-removal contrary gains, unfolding and ordinal endpoint exceptions, and the separate single-seed degree-pair source do not transfer or add their effects to this panel. The chemical associations below make no activation, eligibility, component-contribution or causal-mediation verdict. Reproducible trajectory, component-alias and provenance audits are under runs/SPIRAL2/.slots/r0019-00-improve-L01/molecular/.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1/e262 is a 25-heavy-atom ethyl/methyl/methoxy-substituted fused aromatic carboxamide with a pyridyl group, chlorine directly on the amide nitrogen and fluorine directly on the ring nitrogen. Its nearby tied variants exchange N-Cl and N-F. Seed 0/e240 instead has a 23-heavy-atom partly unsaturated fused/bridged carboxamide with exocyclic unsaturation and an N-chloro pyridyl amide. Seed 2/e280 reaches a 24-heavy-atom fused carbonyl-ring system with an N-amino-N-phenyl carboxamide, without a halogen: an important counterexample to universal dependence on N-halogen chemistry. The initially supplied N-H indole anilide is also conventional recognizable chemistry. Mean proposal SMILES length is 43.1 and halogen-text incidence 0.9414. The Parent had related substituted indole amides, a vicinal-diketone family and a cumulene leader; the Child retains the aromatic/carbonyl organization but reaches different peripheral and ring connectivities. Makeability remains questionable for the N-halogen and crowded additional-ring examples.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl/N-F substitution is distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogen chemistry. The N-N carboxamide of the halogen-free leader is a separate functional environment whose stability is not established.

Seed 2/e272 is the charge-text exception: an N-positive/N-negative double-bond motif, score 0.3235738933994858. It does not establish controlled protonation coverage, and the panel should not be described as universally charge-free.

Dense ring fusion and unusual unsaturation remain geometry questions even when the raw score is high; the largest linked example is also a very low-scoring counterexample to automatic benefit from elaboration.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement are not consistently represented among the leading seed-1 variants. The N-H initial compound and halogen-free seed-2 leader demonstrate that the generator can produce alternatives; the evidence does not justify requiring an N-halogen bond.
The fused and bridged leading graphs do not establish accessible geometry or independently plausible alternatives at the same functional-group arrangement.
The record does not identify an exact absent pharmacophore; these are observed score associations and chemical coverage limits.

This is a raw-score tie, not evidence of equal descriptors or a uniquely required halogen. The halogen-free seed-2 leader scores 0.47360222277831504; lengthening its additional carbonyl ring in e299 scores 0.32507047704275815. A large 49-heavy-atom linked proposal (seed 2/e274) falls to 2.843110302343239e-17, while the late fragment NNF (e300) scores 0.0. Compact combined aromatic/carbonyl organization is associated with the higher values; neither extra atoms nor halogen presence alone explains them. Seed-0's leader scores 0.4450174316132652. Child raw endpoints for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.4450174316132652, 0.4828171386373609 and 0.47360222277831504 versus Parent 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081: all three rise, despite continuing liabilities. An evaluated seed-0 thioether variant (e135, 0.4348637477708051) shares atom-pair counts with an unscored sulfur-H variant; their local similarity is 0.8895027624309392 and mixed similarity 0.9447513812154695. This is component aliasing with only one label, not a scored chemical comparison.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1/e296 is a 35-heavy-atom linked heterocyclic assembly: a nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl-containing aromatic region, chlorovinyl ether, difluoromethyl group, and aminomethyl connection to a methylene-bridged aza-aromatic system bearing tert-butyl substitution. Seed 0/e229 is a 30-heavy-atom carbonyl/thione fused nitrogen system with vinyl substitution, heavily carbon-halogenated aza-aromatic attachment and an N-C(F)-N linkage. Seed 2/e284 is a 37-heavy-atom N-N-linked nitrogen-dione/azole assembly with additional nitrogen-carbonyl functionality, azaaryl side chain and N-Br. Seed 2 also produces much larger repeated dione/azaaryl assemblies, up to 114 heavy-atom tokens across its proposals; mean panel SMILES length is 69.8 and maximum 217. The Parent's leading seed-0 family instead combined an O-F-substituted aza-aromatic region, thione and halomethyl ether. The current seed-1 leader has carbon-bound chlorine/fluorine and no O-F, so that Parent liability is not universal here; linked heterocyclic complexity and local reactive environments remain.
liabilities: The chlorovinyl ether, crowded fused aza-ring junctions, N-C(F)-N linkage and carbonyl/thione chemistry require environment-specific feasibility assessment; the score is not a synthetic route.
Seed-2 leaders add N-Br and N-N connectivity, while very large repeated heterocyclic assemblies increase synthetic complexity without an observed leading-score advantage.
No stereochemical markers resolve saturated bridges or potentially stereogenic halogen-bearing centres.
missing_features: The record does not establish reliable compact, synthetically accessible alternatives to the linked nitrogen-rich ring arrangements across all seeds; the compact seed-1 family shows that very large repeated assemblies are not required.

Stable substitutions preserving the favorable heterocyclic organization remain underdemonstrated in the thione/N-Br and heavily halogenated families. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens are already present and should not be conflated with O-F or N-Br.
Long-range descriptor separation is visible for rearranged dione/azaaryl assemblies, but paired measured scores, verified geometry and chemical feasibility are missing for those split pool pairs.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 1/e266 is a 26-heavy-atom aryl-alkyl tertiary azetidine bearing a second aryl region fused to an oxygen-containing saturated ring with a primary amine and carbon-bound chlorine. The first aromatic region carries a short carbon bridge; its geometry is not established. Nearby near-ceiling relatives instead contain an aziridine and chloromethyl/phenol substitution. Seed 0/e270 is a 30-heavy-atom spiro/polycyclic nitrogen assembly linking two substituted aromatic regions, with methoxy, phenol, aniline and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 2/e299 is a 32-heavy-atom aryl oxo-sulfur-H/azetidine assembly with an additional tertiary aminoalkyl chain and aniline; other high relatives carry aryl hydroperoxide and unusual sulfur-H substitution. Mean proposal SMILES length is 58.5 and halogen-text incidence 0.9885. Basic aliphatic amines are clearly present despite zero formal-charge text incidence. Compared with the Parent's flexible tertiary amine and pyrrolidine/fused-thioether families, the current leaders contain more small nitrogen rings or spiro connectivity. Their recognizable amine/aryl handles do not resolve the local strain and sulfur/peroxide liabilities.
liabilities: Small saturated nitrogen rings and short aromatic carbon bridges need geometry and substitution-specific assessment; azetidine and aziridine should not be treated as interchangeable.
Chloromethyl groups, aryl hydroperoxides and explicit sulfur-H oxo environments are specific reactivity concerns; ordinary aromatic C-Cl/C-F substitution is chemically different.
Near-ceiling raw scores do not demonstrate affinity, selectivity, stability, solubility or a realizable synthesis.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified, geometrically credible versions of the aryl/cyclic-amine arrangements are absent; a chirality-aware descriptor does not supply missing stereochemical assignments.

The record does not establish equivalent-scoring stable alternatives to the chloromethyl, aziridine or unusual sulfur/peroxide environments. Other leaders omit those particular groups, so no single liability is universal.

Protonation states and controlled conformers are unresolved. There is no basis for prescribing an amine simply because formal charge is absent, and the low-scoring initial tertiary amine is a direct counterexample.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0/e275 is a 32-heavy-atom fused aromatic ketone/lactam framework with an alkylated cyclic imino-urea substituent. Current connectivity is different, but large ring closures, crowded junctions and unspecified stereochemistry still make practical synthesis uncertain.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures and multiply connected unsaturated nitrogen systems complicate geometric feasibility and synthesis even at moderate heavy-atom counts.
Some late variants introduce N-O or peroxide functionality; the selected leaders themselves do not require either, and should not inherit every liability of their lower-scoring relatives.
No stereochemical markers occur despite potentially stereogenic bridge and saturated-ring environments.
missing_features: Simpler accessible ring connectivities that reliably retain the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement are not established among the best examples; a smaller high-scoring relative shows that simplification is possible.
Bridged and saturated centres lack specified stereochemical and conformational identity. The absence is chemical definition, not absence of nitrogen or carbonyl functional groups.
The modest score gradients do not identify an exact missing pharmacophore or demonstrate that more rings, acceptors or halogens would help.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2/e292 is a 27-heavy-atom crowded bicyclic enol bearing a direct O-F group and an enlarged aromatic-labelled nitrogen-dione ring with N-F and exocyclic N(F)F. Related high molecules keep fused dione systems and use carbon-bound F or fluoromethyl in place of O-F. liabilities: Direct O-F, ring N-F and exocyclic N(F)F are distinct from ordinary C-F substitution and present substantial reactivity concerns in the leading seed-2 structure.
Enol/diene-rich and enlarged aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings require tautomeric and geometric assessment; parsing and score do not demonstrate a stable isolated compound.
The N-S/formyl-amide family and the large repeated dione low scorer illustrate different chemical liabilities; a single universal halogen or size rule would miss these counterexamples.
missing_features: Chemically stable alternatives that preserve the favorable compact carbonyl/amine/fluorinated organization are not consistently established among the leaders. Carbon-bound fluorine relatives demonstrate that O-F is not universally needed, while the Parent supplies a separate no-N-F endpoint exception under its own chemistry.
The bicyclic and partially unsaturated frameworks lack verified geometry and specified stereochemical identity; graph-distance information cannot establish those properties.
The available observations do not identify an exact absent target-specific motif or show that maximizing fluorine, donors or ring count would improve the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was reproduced by the same-code n-62daf219c70a baseline; it is re-observed, with different molecules, in n-e75f0f495f9b on the complete matched Search Seeds 0/1/2 at 300 observations per task. Current leaders contain N-Cl/N-F/N-Br, O-F, N(F)F, N-S or unusual sulfur-H oxo environments. An evaluated halogen-free aromatic carboxamide reaches 0.47360222277831504, a linked heterocycle leader uses carbon-bound halogens without O-F, and high-scoring aryl cyclic amines use recognizable conventional bonds. These exceptions rule out a universal requirement for reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry or a general inability to form stable bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments around otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need environment-sensitive local alternatives that preserve favorable scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from actual feedback. Distinguish heteroatom-halogen and peroxide chemistry from ordinary carbon-bound halogens or useful amines. These observations motivate checking chemistry; they do not establish that a universal filter improves scores or that the added covariance component caused the liabilities.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The original n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a gap included problematic cyclic unsaturation and bridges. Under the present matched panel, n-e75f0f495f9b instead shows short aromatic carbon bridges, aziridine/azetidine variants, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, bicyclic enols and enlarged aromatic-labelled nitrogen rings. Noncumulated leaders and recognizable cyclic amines are counterexamples to a universal unsaturation defect. Ring-text incidence of 0.9529 to 0.9805 demonstrates plentiful ring chemistry, not its geometric feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish representable ring connectivity from credible geometry and accessible synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction and editing need attention to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity while preserving learned favorable functional arrangements. Assess alternative feasible topologies without treating every small ring, fused system or unsaturated ring as forbidden. Two-dimensional atom-pair separation, high scores and aromatic labels cannot establish a realizable conformation, synthesis or a component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This specification gap originated in n-c55c3d520a2c and recurred in n-62daf219c70a. All five current n-e75f0f495f9b stereocentre-text rates remain zero despite saturated amine, fluorinated and bridged centres. The new chirality-aware atom-pair channel splits all six naturally encountered local-count alias pairs, with no observed pair equal in both channels, but most members have no evaluated labels. Atom-pair-only equal/local-unequal pairs remain, and finite descriptor counts do not specify unassigned stereochemistry. One current charge-separated nitrogen example also prevents describing the output as entirely charge-free; neutral basic amines are visibly present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output leaves potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres unspecified and does not establish a complete molecular identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve chemically relevant stereochemistry during generation, with separate treatment of protonation, tautomerism and configurationally unstable cases. Keep exact molecular identity and geometry distinct from component or mixed similarity. This is an output-definition gap, not a measured stereochemical penalty, proof of remaining joint aliases in this panel, or evidence that further descriptor expansion raises endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap was recorded in n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a and is re-observed under the present complete matched panel. Late tiny fragments reach raw floors, including a three-atom nitrogen/fluorine fragment and ethene at 0.0. An 80-heavy-atom nitrogen-dione assembly scores 0.5910185045885361 versus its seed's 37-atom leader at 0.5984298101710803; a 51-atom elaboration elsewhere scores 0.16401724178840402 versus a 34-atom leader at 0.20763082877093567. Conversely a shorter linked relative retains 0.2069801413741259, and a compact halogen-free aromatic carboxamide performs well. Size alone neither defines useful context nor orders the scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use only task-local observed feedback to preserve useful functional relationships during simplification or replacement and to recognize unhelpful repetition. Retain the possibility of productive small molecules and scaffold simplification. These examples do not justify fixed minimum sizes, automatic preference for larger graphs or a causal claim that covariance changes created the context loss.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This conditional coverage gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c/n-62daf219c70a and persists in the current finite Search panel: many leading examples vary halogens, short side chains, carbonyl-adjacent groups or ring segments within aromatic amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged nitrogen-carbonyl families. Different seeds do produce distinct families, so structural diversity is moderate rather than collapsed. Current unscored pool aliases show that additional arrangements are proposed and six local-count pairs are separated by the mixed representation; they do not demonstrate useful independent scored alternatives. Historical unfolding's nine joint-scope pairs and ordinal's six published pool pairs versus nine wider joint-scope pairs retain their original scopes and cannot be counted as independent efficacy evidence for this Child.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent plausible alternatives to each seed’s leading framework.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek feasible scaffold alternatives that retain favorable chemical relationships learned from real feedback, and assess their actual scores without equating distinct strings, descriptor separation or passive reference choices with useful diversity. Keep this as condition-bound chemical coverage guidance; it neither establishes a universal diversity benefit nor assigns convergence to a particular inherited or added component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
